header.running_head: What Masaajid are Built for and what the Sahabah (RA) did therein

blocks.text: Hadhrat Abul Qamraa (RA) relates, "We were once sitting in several gatherings in Rasulullaah ﷺ's Masjid, discussing Ahadeeth when Rasulullaah ﷺ came out from one of his rooms. Looking at the various gatherings, Rasulullaah ﷺ sat down with those busy with (learning and teaching) the Qur'aan. He then said, 'I have been commanded to sit with this gathering.'" [^1]
The Statement of Hadhrat Ali (RA) Concerning the Qurraa of the Qur'aan

Hadhrat Kulayb bin Shihaab narrates that Hadhrat Ali (RA) once heard a lot of sound from the Masjid as people were busy reciting the Qur'aan and teaching others to do so. He remarked, "Glad tidings for these people! These are the people whom Rasulullaah ﷺ loved the most." [^2]

It is also Hadhrat Kulayb who narrates that Hadhrat Ali (RA) was once in the Masjid of Kufa when he heard a lot of sound. "Who is that?" he asked. When he was informed that the sound was coming from some people who were busy reciting or learning the Qur'aan, he commented, "Take note that it was such people whom Rasulullaah ﷺ loved most." [^3]
The Incident of Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) with the People in the Market place

Hadhrat Hasan reports that Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) once passed through the market place of Madinah when he stood there and called out, "O traders! What makes you so helpless?" "What are you talking about, O Abu Hurayrah (RA)?" they asked. He said, "There you have the inheritance of Rasulullaah ﷺ being distributed whereas you people are still here! Are you not going to claim your shares?" "Where is it?" they all asked. "In the Masjid," he replied. They all rushed to the Masjid as Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) remained there waiting for them. When they returned (and he noted the despondency on their faces), he asked, "What is the matter?" "O Abu Hurayrah (RA)!" they replied, "We went to the Masjid but found nothing being distributed there." Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) asked, "Did you see absolutely no one there?" "O yes we did," they replied, "we saw some people performing salaah, others reciting the Qur'aan and others discussing what was Halaal and what was Haraam." Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) remarked, "Shame on you! That is the inheritance if Rasulullaah ﷺ." [^4]

Ibn Mandah, as quoted in Isaabah (Vol.4 Pg.160). Ibn Abdul Birr has also reported the narration in his Isti'aab (Vol.4 Pg.164), as has Abu Amr Daani in his Tabaqaattul Qurraa, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.219).

Tabraani in his Awsat, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id (Vol.7 Pg.166). Haythami has however commented on the chain of narrators. Ibn Munee has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.218).
